$comment: An OpenAPI-like description of commands, not HTTP. Read it with the "Reading contract.json" section of README.md.
name: The agent contract
description: The commands between the referee and an agent adapter, as they stand. Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-23. README.md beside this file has the sequence diagrams, the mapping for each agent, and the reasons.

transport.stdin: One JSON object, matching the command's stdin schema.
transport.stdout: One JSON object, matching the command's stdout schema, written in full before the process exits.
transport.stderr: Progress and the reason for exit 2. Never part of the answer.

exitCodes.0: An answer on stdout. Every decision is inside it, refusals included.
exitCodes.2: The input does not match the stdin schema, or its version is not this one. A bug in the caller. One sentence on stderr, nothing on stdout.
exitCodes.other: No answer: any other exit code, a timeout, or stdout that does not match. Each command’s ifNoAnswer describes the fallback.

transport.version: Every request and answer carries the harness schema version printed by workflow version.
transport.messages: Every message is { code, for, text }. The agent sees every message; for: operator means the operator must see it too. An adapter shows the text of a code it does not know, so adding a code breaks nothing. text is Markdown.
transport.paths: Paths in stdin are as the agent gave them: from the repository root, or absolute. The referee resolves them.
transport.refusedRulebook: A rulebook the referee refuses is an answer, not a crash: every moment answers one stop message for the operator naming the key and the reason, and denies what it would otherwise decide.

on write.description:
Called before every tool call that may write: file edits, and shell
commands. The adapter turns its agent's tool call into `writes` and,
for a shell call, passes the command line in `command`.

The referee decides, in this order:

1. A locked path is denied, as is a delete under the requirements
   folder. The locks are the referee's own (`.katatay/`, `.git/`) and
   the rulebook's `agent.lockedPaths`.
2. A path outside the repository is allowed.
3. A file directly in the rulebook's `plans.dir`, not in a
   subfolder, or the follow-ups file, is allowed in every phase.
4. A broken logbook denies every other write.
5. In phase `open`, every other write is denied.

For `command`, the referee applies rule b: deny when the command names a
locked path together with a write marker (`>`, `>>`, `rm`, `mv`, `cp`,
`tee`, `sed -i`, `truncate`). A command is never a phase-gated write.
An edit made through the shell is caught when the turn ends.
on write.stdoutMeans: The decision. `messages` is empty when allowed, and holds one message saying why when denied.
on write.ifNoAnswer: The adapter denies every file write, plans and the follow-ups file included, and allows a shell command.

messages.text: No plan has been approved on this branch, so edits are not permitted yet. Present a plan for the operator to approve.

on prompt.description:
Records `record` and `reset` when the whole message is one of them, and
always ends with a `state` message saying where the change stands. The
referee also asks the adapter's `check` here, and returns each warning as
a `warning` message for the operator.
on prompt.stdoutMeans: Messages only. A prompt is never refused here.
on prompt.ifNoAnswer: The adapter puts "workflow: state unavailable" and the reason in front of the agent. The prompt still goes through.

on plan-presented.description: A courtesy using the same validator as turn end. Reads the plan and returns diagnostics without writing state, granting approval or running phase work. A valid plan is silent. The adapter bounds correction requests and warns when no answer is available.
on plan-presented.stdoutMeans: Whether plan contents need correction, and what to say. This is not a permission decision.
on plan-presented.ifNoAnswer: Warn and continue presentation; never approve or permanently block the operator’s dialog.

on plan-approved.description:
The only way a change gets permission to start. Call it only when the
operator really approved; how the adapter knows is its own business.

Before calling, the adapter makes sure `planFile` exists, sits directly in
the rulebook's `plans.dir`, and holds the plan the operator approved,
with any edits they made. A revised plan may reuse the file of the approval
before it.

The referee reads the plan from the file, checks its format (its
closing `workflow` block, such as `test-only:` and `requirement-changes:`), pins the
baseline on a first approval, publishes the exact bytes and appends
`plan_approved` with the proposal hash, snapshot reference, declarations and baseline.

It answers `recorded: false` with `refused` on the target branch, for changed content on a
branch whose change is already recorded, and on a plan whose format
does not check out. It answers `recorded: false` with `stop` when the
file is missing or not directly in `plans.dir`, when no baseline can be
pinned, or when the snapshot cannot be published.

Approving byte-identical content to the current live grant returns recorded: false with an informational message and changes no state. A different plan follows revision rules. Reset and merge end the live grant.
on plan-approved.ifNoAnswer: The adapter tells the operator no new approval was recorded; the existing phase still applies.

on turn-end.description:
Adapters should send planFile when a turn presents a plan. This courtesy helps the operator see problems before approving; approval does not depend on it. Collect plan problems, then run ordinary turn-end work and return both sets of messages. The courtesy never replaces the freeze check, verification, mutation or recording. Invalid contents receive correction instructions through the existing one-shot keepWorking mechanism. Capture failures and unreadable or misplaced plan files are warnings. Successful validation is silent and grants no permission. The Claude adapter checks before ExitPlanMode through on plan-presented; the Codex adapter checks at turn end. Template validation defaults on through plans.validateFormat; YAML and declaration checks always apply. Approval does not rerun template validation or require a receipt.

Holds the freeze, runs verify itself, runs mutation once per plan,
records the change once declared, and says what comes next.

`keepWorking: true` means the agent has more work to do and the turn
may not end yet: the adapter makes the agent carry on with the
messages. A pass that only has something to tell the operator, such
as `verified`, answers `keepWorking: false`; delivering it is the
adapter's job, and an adapter may refuse the stop to do that.

A fresh triage reply can request convergence once. A stop used to deliver triage or a verification pass still leaves one opportunity to request fixes after verification fails. Verify is not run again when the tree is
unchanged since the last `verify_failed` in the logbook, on any turn end.
on turn-end.stdoutMeans: Whether the agent must keep working, and what to say.
on turn-end.ifNoAnswer: The adapter says nothing was verified, and keeps the agent working unless stopRefusedBefore was true.

messages.text:
Verification passed and was recorded against this working tree.

Test quality on the lines this change touched: …

Where review should look: …

check.summary: What is wrong with the agent's setup?
check.description:
Asked on every prompt and by `state:show` and `state:verify`. Warnings
never fail anything: only the operator can fix the agent's settings.
The referee turns each one into a `warning` message for the operator. No
answer becomes one more warning, which the referee writes itself.
check.stdoutMeans: The warnings. Empty when nothing is wrong.
check.ifNoAnswer: The referee adds one warning of its own saying the check gave no answer. Silence is never read as a clean report.

defaults.run: the adapter's defaults command, which init is pointed at
defaults.summary: What init should propose for this agent.
defaults.description:
Asked once, by `init`, which writes the answer into the draft rulebook
and the operator's to-do list. Nothing reads it afterwards: from then
on the rulebook is the operator's.

`init` runs where no rulebook exists yet, so it is told which adapter
to use and finds this command there. It then writes the adapter's
check command into the draft rulebook.
defaults.ifNoAnswer: init leaves the agent's part of the draft rulebook empty and tells the operator why.

steps: Check the hooks merged into .claude/settings.json. The file is locked, so a session cannot change them.
Start a new Claude Code session afterwards, so it loads the new hooks.

install.summary: Which files carry the workflow's instructions and skills for this agent, and how are its hooks registered?
install.description:
Asked by `init`, which writes the files it answers and never overwrites one. A file marked `shared` holds the project's own text too: when it exists, `init` appends the workflow's text between marker lines instead. The `registration` is the agent's hook registration file, whole, after the adapter merged the workflow's hooks into what the project's file holds. `init` writes it, the one locked path it may write, because the operator runs `init`.

The request carries the referee's texts: its instructions and the harness
support skills. A project has no copy of the harness, so the adapter reads
none of its files, and nothing it installs points back into the harness.
The adapter turns the texts into its agent's format and location, and may
reword them as it wishes.

The referee refuses a path that is absolute, leaves the project, or that a
lock covers: its own, or the agent's locked paths from its defaults.
install.stdoutMeans: The files to write, and the hook registration.
install.ifNoAnswer: init installs no instructions, no skills and no hooks for this agent, and tells the operator why.

Version.description: The contract's version. Any other number is input that does not match.

Audience.description:
The agent sees every message. `operator` means the operator must see
it too, and how is the adapter's choice. A string so that a third
audience can be added later.

Code.description:
One list for every moment. A code names a situation someone handles
differently. An adapter shows the text of a code it does not know.

meanings.state: where the change stands, on every prompt
meanings.warning: the operator judges it, including the agent's setup
meanings.stop: only the operator can fix it
meanings.refused: fix the plan or the branch, present again
meanings.declared: write the change file; carries the change report
meanings.held: the operator types record again to declare
meanings.frozen: unwind the test edits, then run triage
meanings.run_triage: run triage, now or when the implementation is done
meanings.triaged: repeat the buckets to the operator
meanings.verify_failed: repeat the summary to the operator; fix the implementation
meanings.verified: repeat the report; the operator decides on record
meanings.change_file: write or fix the change file
meanings.recorded: write the commit message, wait for yes

text.description: Markdown: paragraphs, lists, inline code. The referee's wording, with no agent's vocabulary.

Messages.description: In the order to show them. Messages never decide anything.

path.description: As the agent gave it: from the repository root, or absolute.

delete.description: True when the call removes the file or moves it away.

WriteRequest.description: At least one of `writes` and `command` is non-empty.

writes.description: Every file the call writes, moves or removes. Empty for a shell call.

command.description: The shell command line, for a shell call. Null otherwise.

prompt.description: The operator's message as they typed it.

PromptAnswer.description: Codes used: state, info, warning, stop, reset, declared, recorded, held, not_declared. The last message is always state, except when the state cannot be read at all: then the answer is one stop.

planFile.description:
The plan the operator approved: a Markdown file directly in the
rulebook's `plans.dir`, holding the approved text with any edits. The referee
reads the plan from here and records the snapshot reference and the hash.

PlanApprovedAnswer.description: Codes used: approved, refused, run_triage, info, warning, stop.

recorded.description: Whether a new approval event was recorded. False also represents an already-approved identical plan, with an info message and the existing phase preserved.

stopRefusedBefore.description:
True when an earlier stop in this turn was refused, by the referee's
keepWorking or by the adapter delivering a message. Claude's and
Codex's stop_hook_active. Used only to stop a turn looping.

secondsLeft.description: How long the agent still gives this hook before killing it. Mutation starts only when the rulebook's whole time limit fits, with 20 seconds to spare.

triageReplyId.description: Optional identifier of this final triage reply, stable across overlapping stops. For the newly triaged tree it requests one continuation before verification. An ordinary completion omits it.

planFile.description: Adapters should send this optional path when a turn presents a plan: a readable Markdown file directly in plans.dir. Omitted or null skips this courtesy. It helps the operator see problems before approving; approval does not depend on it. The referee checks template structure (unless plans.validateFormat is false) and declarations, and combines the messages with phase-specific results. It never replaces the freeze check, verification, mutation or recording, grants no approval and creates no receipt. Unreadable or misplaced files are warnings. The Claude adapter checks before ExitPlanMode through on plan-presented; the Codex adapter checks at turn end.

TurnEndAnswer.description: Codes used: refused, info, warning, stop, frozen, run_triage, triaged, verify_failed, verified, change_file, recorded.

extraHooks.description: This adapter's extraHooks settings from agent.adapters.<name>. Null when its check is switched off, and then the adapter reports no extra hooks. Missing and switched-off workflow hooks are reported either way.

warnings.description: Each a sentence for the operator, who has no other context.

locked.description: The agent's own config, as globs. `~` is the home directory. Becomes the rulebook's agent.lockedPaths.

plansFolder.description: Where this agent keeps plans. Becomes the rulebook's plans.dir.

instructions.description: The file this agent reads the workflow's instructions from. The install command writes it, and check warns when it is missing.

commands.description: The adapter's commands, as command lines run from the project root. init writes check to agent.adapters.<name>.checkCommand and runs install during setup.

registration.description: The agent's hook registration: the file, the hooks it holds, and the steps only the operator can take. init writes the file from the install answer's registration, merged into what the project already has, and prints the steps.

text.description: The hook registration to merge into that file.

steps.description: Anything else only the operator can do, such as trusting the hooks in Codex with /hooks.

plansFolder.description: The rulebook's plans folder, `~` for the home directory, for an agent whose own settings name where plans go.

instructions.description: The workflow's instructions, in words any agent can follow.

description.description: What the skill is for, which an agent reads to decide when to use it.

path.description: From the project root. Never absolute, never outside the project, never locked.

shared.description: The project's own text shares this file. An existing one gets the workflow's text appended between marker lines, never replaced.

registration.description: The hook registration file, whole, with the workflow's hooks merged into what the project's file holds. Its path is the defaults answer's registration.file.
